## Critique
- claim-1: The bounded excerpt supports the integral in-box Schur basis and identifies the inspected source, revision, and stable locator.
- claim-2: The quotient-basis deduction is valid because the out-of-box Schur span is both an ideal and a direct summand of the integral Schur basis.
- claim-3: Correctly identifies the missing evidence. The cited excerpts state neither quotient Littlewood–Richardson multiplication nor its Pieri specialization.
- claim-4: Correct conclusion: only the basis portion is established; the requested combined source certificate is not established. No parent-theorem conclusion follows.

## Repair certificates
- [source-refresh] Supply a stable formal-source excerpt, with exact bounded locators, stating the quotient formulas
  \[
  \bar s_\lambda\bar s_\mu=\sum_{\nu\subseteq(n-r)^r}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\bar s_\nu
  \]
  and
  \[
  \bar h_k\bar s_\lambda=
  \sum_{\substack{\nu\subseteq(n-r)^r\\ \nu/\lambda\text{ horizontal }k\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\nu,
  \]
  including all hypotheses and the convention that out-of-box terms vanish.

## Required revisions
- Retain the explicit conclusion that the source certificate remains unestablished until the quotient LR/Pieri excerpt is supplied.
